llm.summary: This skill clearly discloses that it connects to a Kia account to read vehicle data and run user-confirmed vehicle commands, including sensitive actions like location lookup and door unlocking.

dimensions.detail: Requested environment values are limited to Kia account credentials and optional Kia-specific write mode, device id, and token settings needed for the integration.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses an MCP config invoking `npx -y kiaaccess-mcp`; this is disclosed and normal for an MCP integration, though users should recognize it fetches and runs the npm package rather than only using the markdown skill text.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions repeatedly require explicit user confirmation for commands, warn not to guess vehicle keys or retry bad logins, and distinguish dry runs from executed actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses long-lived local remember-me token storage and a confirm-gated plaintext token export; this is sensitive but purpose-aligned and explicitly described.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The capabilities are high impact because they involve a real vehicle, account credentials, location, charging, climate, and optional door lock/unlock commands, but they directly match the stated Kia Access purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an agent to access your Kia account and potentially control vehicle functions. Use `KIA_WRITE_MODE=none` for read-only access, keep the default or stricter mode unless you need commands, and use `all` only if you accept confirm-gated door lock/unlock authority. Treat the Kia password and exported refresh token like full account credentials.
